title: Which data structure follows the LIFO (Last In First Out) principle?
explanation: A Stack processes elements in LIFO order (Push and Pop operate on the top element).

title: What is the average time complexity of searching an item in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
explanation: In a balanced BST, height is log(n), making search, insertion, and deletion O(log n).

title: Which HTTP method is idempotent according to RFC standards?
explanation: PUT operations are idempotent because repeating the same request produces the same server state.

title: What does ACID stand for in Database Management Systems?
explanation: ACID guarantees database transaction reliability.

title: Which sorting algorithm has the best worst-case time complexity?
explanation: Merge Sort guarantees O(n log n) time complexity in all cases (worst, average, best).

title: Which layer of the OSI model handles routing and packet forwarding?
explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) handles logical addressing and packet routing across networks.

title: What is the default port number for HTTPS communication?
explanation: Port 443 is the standard port for TLS/SSL encrypted HTTPS traffic.

title: Which memory allocation mechanism causes external fragmentation?
explanation: Contiguous allocation leads to scattered free memory blocks that are too small individually.

title: What is the purpose of the 'git rebase' command?
options: Reapplies commits on top of another base tip
explanation: Rebase moves or combines a sequence of commits to a new base commit for a linear history.

title: Which design pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally?
explanation: Singleton pattern restricts instantiation of a class to a single object instance.

title: What is the time complexity of accessing an array element by index?
explanation: Arrays offer constant O(1) time complexity access via memory offset calculation.

title: In C++, which keyword prevents a class method from being overridden in derived classes?
explanation: The 'final' specifier prevents virtual methods from being overridden.

title: Which SQL clause is used to filter aggregated group records?
explanation: HAVING filters groups created by GROUP BY, while WHERE filters individual rows.

title: What is a deadlock condition where processes wait circularly for resources?
explanation: Circular wait occurs when a closed chain of processes each holds a resource needed by the next.

title: Which graph algorithm finds the shortest path from a single source node to all others in non-negative weighted graphs?
explanation: Dijkstra algorithm computes single-source shortest paths for non-negative edge weights.

title: What type of parsing does a YACC compiler generator use?
explanation: YACC generates LALR(1) bottom-up syntax parsers.

title: In IPv4 addressing, how many bits long is an IP address?
explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits (4 octets) long.

title: Which data structure is used to implement a Breadth-First Search (BFS) graph traversal?
explanation: BFS uses a FIFO Queue to visit neighbor nodes level by level.

title: What does the CAP theorem state for distributed systems?
explanation: CAP theorem proves a distributed system can only provide 2 out of 3 guarantees simultaneously.

title: Which garbage collection algorithm identifies unreachable objects starting from root references?
explanation: Mark and Sweep traces live objects from roots and sweeps unreachable memory.

title: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height 'h'?
explanation: A full binary tree of height h contains 2^(h+1) - 1 nodes.

title: In OOP, what is polymorphism?
options: Ability of objects to take many forms
explanation: Polymorphism allows methods to behave differently based on the calling object instance.

title: What protocol operates at the Transport layer to provide reliable stream connection?
explanation: TCP provides reliable, connection-oriented, ordered byte-stream delivery.

title: What is the time complexity of building a heap from an unsorted array of n elements?
explanation: Build-Heap using bottom-up heapify takes O(n) linear time.

title: Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives the lowest average waiting time?
explanation: SJF is mathematically optimal for minimizing average waiting time.

title: What is a closure in JavaScript?
options: A function combined with references to its surrounding lexical state
A method that closes a file handle
explanation: A closure gives an inner function access to an outer function's scope even after outer returns.

title: Which normal form eliminates partial functional dependencies?
explanation: 2NF requires 1NF and no non-prime attribute dependent on a subset of any candidate key.

title: Which tool converts high-level source code directly into machine object code?
explanation: Compilers translate entire high-level source files into machine/assembly code.

title: What is the space complexity of an in-place Quick Sort algorithm?
explanation: In-place Quick Sort uses O(log n) stack space for recursive calls.

title: Which security attack tricks a browser into sending unauthorized requests to a trusted site?
explanation: CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) forces logged-in end users to execute unwanted actions.

title: Which of the following is known as the 'Father of Scientific Management'?
explanation: F.W. Taylor pioneered Scientific Management principles in industrial manufacturing.

title: What does the 4 Ps of Marketing mix stand for?
explanation: E. Jerome McCarthy introduced Product, Price, Place, and Promotion in 1960.

title: In Financial Management, what does NPV stand for?
explanation: NPV is the difference between current value of cash inflows and outflows over time.

title: Who formulated the 'Hierarchy of Needs' theory of human motivation?
explanation: Maslow proposed the 5-tier pyramid of human needs from physiological to self-actualization.

title: What does SWOT analysis stand for?
explanation: SWOT evaluates internal Strengths & Weaknesses alongside external Opportunities & Threats.

title: Which financial statement summarizes revenues, expenses, and net profit over a specific period?
explanation: Income Statement measures business financial performance over an accounting period.

title: What is Theory X and Theory Y developed by Douglas McGregor?
options: Leadership styles based on employee motivation assumptions
explanation: Theory X assumes workers dislike work; Theory Y assumes workers are self-motivated.

title: Which ratio measures a firm's ability to pay off short-term obligations with quick assets?
explanation: Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory) / Current Liabilities.

title: What is 'Kanban' in Lean Operations Management?
options: A visual scheduling system for inventory and production control
explanation: Kanban signals production workflow steps using visual cards to minimize WIP inventory.

title: Which organizational structure groups employees based on specialized functional roles?
explanation: Functional structure organizes by departments (Finance, Marketing, HR, R&D).

title: What is the Break-Even Point in cost accounting?
options: Point where total revenues equal total costs
Point where fixed costs equal zero
explanation: Break-even occurs when total revenue equals total fixed plus variable costs (zero profit/loss).

title: What does BCG Matrix classify business units into?
options: Stars, Cash Cows, Question Marks, Dogs
explanation: BCG matrix plots market growth rate against relative market share.

title: What is Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR)?
options: A company's sense of responsibility towards community and environment
explanation: CSR is a business model where companies assess social and environmental impacts.

title: Who proposed the 14 Principles of Management?
explanation: Henri Fayol published 14 principles of general administrative management.

title: What is 'Span of Control' in organizational management?
options: Number of subordinates directly supervised by a manager
Time required to complete a project
explanation: Span of control defines how many subordinates report directly to a executive/manager.

title: Which pricing strategy sets a high initial price and lowers it over time?
explanation: Price skimming targets early adopters willing to pay premium prices initially.

title: What is the DuPont Analysis framework used for evaluating?
explanation: DuPont splits ROE into Profit Margin, Asset Turnover, and Financial Leverage.

title: What does Just-In-Time (JIT) manufacturing aim to reduce?
explanation: JIT receives materials only as needed in production, cutting storage waste.

title: What is a 'Hostile Takeover' in corporate finance?
options: Acquisition of a target company without management approval
explanation: A hostile takeover acquires control by buying shares directly from stockholders.

title: What does PESTEL analysis evaluate?
options: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal factors
Product, Expense, Sales, Trade, Earnings, Leverage
People, Excellence, Service, Team, Ethics, Leadership
Price, Equity, Stock, Tax, Economy, Liquidity
explanation: PESTEL analyzes external macro-environmental influences on business strategy.

title: In Human Resource Management, what is '360-degree feedback'?
options: Performance evaluation from peers, managers, subordinates, and self
explanation: 360-degree feedback gathers performance reviews from all surrounding workplace contacts.

title: What is the Primary Market in stock exchanges?
options: Market where new securities are issued for the first time (IPO)
Market for trading existing shares between investors
explanation: Primary market handles initial public offerings (IPOs) directly from issuers.

title: Who introduced the Two-Factor Theory (Motivators & Hygiene factors)?
explanation: Herzberg distinguished job motivators from hygiene dissatisfaction factors.

title: What is 'Economies of Scale'?
options: Cost advantages reaped by companies when production becomes efficient
Increasing price per unit with higher volume
Loss of money due to expanding factories
explanation: Per-unit fixed cost drops as output production volume grows.

title: Which financial metric measures operating cash generated per dollar of revenue?
explanation: OCF Margin measures how efficiently revenue converts to actual cash flow.

title: What is Porter's Five Forces model used for analyzing?
explanation: Michael Porter's 5 forces assess competitive pressures within an industry.

title: What is a 'Balance Sheet' fundamental equation?
explanation: The accounting equation mandates Assets must equal total Liabilities plus Equity.

title: What is 'Benchmarking' in quality management?
options: Comparing business processes and performance metrics to industry bests
explanation: Benchmarking measures company practices against leading peer benchmarks.

title: In project management, what is the 'Critical Path'?
options: Longest sequence of dependent tasks determining minimum project duration
The cheapest path to complete a task
explanation: Critical Path method identifies zero-float tasks that directly delay total project completion.

title: What does CRM stand for in business operations?
explanation: CRM systems manage company interactions and data across customer lifecycles.

title: Which enzyme is commonly known as 'molecular scissors' in Recombinant DNA Technology?
explanation: Restriction Enzymes cut DNA strands at specific target palindrome sequences.

title: Which technique is used for amplifying specific DNA sequences in vitro?
explanation: Kary Mullis invented PCR to generate millions of copies of a target DNA region.

title: What vector is most commonly used for gene transfer into dicotyledonous plant cells?
explanation: Agrobacterium's Ti plasmid naturally transfers T-DNA into plant plant genomes.

title: Which blot technique is used specifically for the detection of RNA sequences?
explanation: Northern Blot detects RNA, Southern detects DNA, and Western detects Proteins.

title: What is the primary function of DNA Ligase enzyme in molecular cloning?
options: Joining DNA fragments by forming phosphodiester bonds
explanation: DNA Ligase seals single-strand nicks by catalyzing phosphodiester bond formation.

title: Which cell organelle is known as the powerhouse of eukaryotic cells?
explanation: Mitochondria generate energy through ATP oxidative phosphorylation.

title: What is Monoclonal Antibody production technology called?
explanation: Kohler & Milstein developed hybridoma technology fusing B-cells with myeloma cells.

title: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA but absent in DNA?
explanation: Uracil replaces Thymine in RNA molecules.

title: What is the function of CRISPR-Cas9 system in gene editing?
options: Targeted genome editing and sequence cutting
explanation: CRISPR-Cas9 uses guide RNA to precisely edit genomic target sites.

title: Which protein structure level represents the 3D folding of a single polypeptide chain?
explanation: Tertiary structure is the complete 3D spatial conformation of a polypeptide chain.

title: What is cDNA synthesized from during reverse transcription?
explanation: Reverse transcriptase converts mRNA templates into complementary DNA (cDNA).

title: Which technique separates biomolecules based on their charge-to-mass ratio using electric current?
explanation: Gel electrophoresis moves charged nucleic acids or proteins through a matrix under electricity.

title: What is the start codon for protein synthesis in universal genetic code?
explanation: AUG codes for Methionine and serves as the translation start signal.

title: Which fermentation type operates continuously by feeding fresh media and removing broth?
explanation: Continuous culture maintains steady steady-state growth by constant feed and drain.

title: What is totipotency in plant tissue culture?
options: Ability of a single plant cell to regenerate into a whole organism
explanation: Gottlieb Haberlandt defined totipotency as the capacity of a cell to develop into a complete plant.

title: Which instrument measures light absorption by solute molecules in solution?
explanation: Spectrophotometers quantify light intensity absorbance according to Beer-Lambert law.

title: What is the role of SDS (Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate) in SDS-PAGE electrophoresis?
options: Imparts negative charge and denatures proteins
explanation: SDS denatures proteins and confers a uniform negative charge-to-mass ratio.

title: Which virus is commonly used as a expression vector in insect cell culture?
explanation: Baculoviruses (Autographa californica) express high yields of recombinant protein in Sf9 cells.

title: What is the primary site of protein synthesis in eukaryotic cells?
explanation: Ribosomes translate mRNA sequences into amino acid peptide chains.

title: Which enzyme unwinds double-stranded DNA during replication?
explanation: DNA Helicase breaks hydrogen bonds between bases to open the replication fork.

title: What is a Plasmid?
options: Small, circular, extrachromosomal double-stranded DNA in bacteria
explanation: Plasmids are autonomous self-replicating circular DNA molecules used as cloning vectors.

title: Which enzyme prevents DNA supercoiling ahead of the replication fork?
explanation: Topoisomerase relieves torsional strain by cutting and rejoining DNA strands.

title: What is the purpose of enzyme ELISA assay?
options: Detecting and quantifying specific antigens or antibodies
explanation: Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay uses enzyme-labeled antibodies for antigen detection.

title: Which term describes organisms containing foreign genes introduced engineered by biotechnology?
explanation: Transgenic organisms (GMOs) carry stably integrated foreign recombinant genes.

title: What is downstream processing in industrial biotechnology?
options: Recovery, isolation, and purification of biosynthetic products
explanation: Downstream processing handles harvest separation, extraction, purification, and formulation.

title: Which bond stabilizes the alpha-helix secondary structure of proteins?
explanation: Intramolecular hydrogen bonds between backbone N-H and C=O groups stabilize alpha-helices.

title: What is the function of Taq Polymerase in PCR reaction?
options: Heat-stable DNA synthesis at high temperatures
explanation: Taq Polymerase isolated from Thermus aquaticus withstands 95°C denaturation heat.

title: Which post-translational modification involves adding carbohydrate chains to proteins?
explanation: Glycosylation attaches oligosaccharide glycans to amino acid side chains in ER/Golgi.

title: What is Bio-remediation?
options: Use of microorganisms to clean up environmental pollutants
explanation: Bioremediation uses microbes/plants to detoxify hazardous environmental contaminants.

title: Which parameter is measured by Mass Spectrometry?
explanation: Mass specs measure m/z ratios to identify protein/molecule chemical structures.

title: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is known as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution'?
explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the heart & soul of the constitution.

title: What is the Latin maxim 'Mens Rea' defined as in Criminal Law?
explanation: Mens Rea refers to mental intent to commit a crime.

title: Which fundamental right guarantees protection of life and personal liberty in India?
explanation: Article 21 states no person shall be deprived of life or liberty except by procedure established by law.

title: What is 'Actus Reus' in criminal jurisprudence?
explanation: Actus Reus is the physical act or omission that constitutes a crime.

title: Which landmark Supreme Court case established the 'Basic Structure Doctrine'?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
explanation: The 1973 Kesavananda verdict ruled Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of Constitution.

title: Under Indian Contract Act 1872, an agreement enforceable by law is a:
explanation: Section 2(h) defines a contract as an agreement enforceable by law.

title: What is the minimum age to qualify for election as the President of India?
explanation: Article 58 sets 35 years as the minimum age requirement for presidential candidates.

title: What is a 'Tort' in civil legal jurisprudence?
options: A civil wrong independent of contract for which unliquidated damages are claimed
explanation: Torts are civil wrongs remedies by civil court action for damages.

title: Which writ is issued by a court asking an authority to produce a detained person?
explanation: Habeas Corpus literally means 'to have the body' to check illegal detention.

title: What does PIL stand for in legal practice?
explanation: PIL allows public-spirited individuals to file cases for community justice.

title: Which Part of the Indian Constitution contains Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)?
explanation: Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) lays down DPSP principles for governance.

title: What is 'Ratio Decidendi' in court judgments?
options: The legal reason/principle for the decision
explanation: Ratio Decidendi is the binding legal reasoning that forms judicial precedent.

title: Under IPC, what is the age of criminal responsibility below which an infant cannot be convicted?
explanation: Section 82 IPC provides absolute immunity (Doli incapax) to children under 7.

title: What does 'Audi Alteram Partem' mean?
options: No one shall be judge in his own cause
Ignorance of law is no excuse
explanation: Audi alteram partem is a core natural justice principle requiring fair hearing of both sides.

title: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced Fundamental Duties into Article 51A?
explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act 1976 added Fundamental Duties based on Swaran Singh Committee.

title: What is the maximum period an emergency under Article 356 (President's Rule) can remain in force with approval?
options: 6 months at a time up to 3 years
explanation: President's Rule requires parliamentary approval every 6 months up to a 3-year cap.

title: Under Indian Evidence Act, what is 'Hearsay Evidence'?
options: Second-hand evidence not directly witnessed by the testifying witness
explanation: Hearsay is generally inadmissible as witnesses must testify to facts perceived by themselves.

title: What is 'Bailment' under Law of Contracts?
options: Delivery of goods by one person to another for a purpose under contract
explanation: Section 148 defines bailment as delivery of goods upon condition of return or disposal.

title: Which Article abolishes Untouchability in India?
explanation: Article 17 explicitly abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice.

title: What is 'Voire Dire' in court proceedings?
options: Preliminary examination of a witness or juror to test competency
explanation: Voir dire tests truthfulness or qualification of prospective jurors/witnesses.

title: Which authority is the apex court of appeal in India?
explanation: The Supreme Court under Article 124 is the highest judicial court and final court of appeal.

title: What is 'Quasi-Contract'?
options: An obligation imposed by law resembling a contract without formal agreement
explanation: Quasi-contracts prevent unjust enrichment where law creates contractual duties.

title: Which Schedule of Indian Constitution lists official languages?
explanation: The 8th Schedule lists the 22 recognized official regional languages of India.

title: What is 'Cognizable Offense' under Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC)?
options: An offense in which police can arrest without a warrant
explanation: Cognizable offenses allow police to initiate investigation and arrest without judicial warrant.

title: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor of an Indian state?
options: Chief Justice of the concerned High Court
explanation: Article 159 mandates oath administration by the Chief Justice of the state High Court.

title: What is 'Res Judicata'?
options: A matter already settled by judgment cannot be re-litigated between same parties
explanation: Section 11 CPC prevents re-trying cases on issues already decided between same parties.

title: What is the term of office for a Judge of the Supreme Court of India?
options: Until attaining the age of 65 years
explanation: Supreme Court judges hold office until age 65 (High Court judges until 62).

title: Which Article deals with Constitutional Amendments in India?
explanation: Article 368 grants Parliament power to amend the Constitution and procedure thereof.

title: What is 'Vicarious Liability'?
options: Liability of one person for the tortious acts committed by another
explanation: Master-servant or employer-employee relationships create vicarious liability for workplace torts.

title: Which body recommends distribution of tax revenues between Centre and States?
explanation: Article 280 requires setting up a Finance Commission every 5 years for tax distribution.

title: Which organ is the primary site of drug metabolism in the human body?
explanation: The liver contains Cytochrome P450 enzymes that metabolize xenobiotics and drugs.

title: What does 'p.o.' mean on a medical prescription dosage instruction?
explanation: Per os (p.o.) is Latin for oral administration via mouth.

title: Which class of drugs does Aspirin belong to?
explanation: Acetylsalicylic acid (Aspirin) is an NSAID that inhibits COX-1 and COX-2 enzymes.

title: What is Bioavailability of a drug?
options: Fraction of unchanged drug that reaches systemic circulation
explanation: Bioavailability measures rate and extent of active drug entering systemic bloodstream.

title: Which schedule under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules lists Prescription Drugs?
explanation: Schedule H drugs cannot be sold across retail counter without registered practitioner prescription.

title: What is the antidote for Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) poisoning overdose?
explanation: NAC restores hepatic glutathione stores to neutralize toxic NAPQI metabolite.

title: Which organelle is responsible for drug detoxifying Cytochrome P450 enzyme synthesis?
explanation: Smooth ER in hepatocytes houses CYP450 enzymes responsible for phase-I metabolism.

title: What is the mechanism of action of Penicillin antibiotics?
options: Inhibition of bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan synthesis
explanation: Penicillins bind transpeptidase (PBP) to prevent bacterial cell wall cross-linking.

title: What does Pharmacokinetics study?
options: What the body does to the drug (ADME)
What the drug does to the body
explanation: Pharmacokinetics analyzes Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion (ADME).

title: Which dosage form is designed to bypass first-pass liver metabolism completely?
explanation: IV administration injects drug directly into systemic veins, completely avoiding gut/liver first-pass.

title: What is the half-life (t1/2) of a drug?
options: Time required for plasma drug concentration to decrease by 50%
Time to absorb half the tablet
explanation: Elimination half-life is the duration needed for systemic drug concentration to reduce by half.

title: Which natural alkaloid isolated from Cinchona bark is used to treat Malaria?
explanation: Quinine is an antimalarial alkaloid extracted from Cinchona tree bark.

title: What is the therapeutic index of a drug?
options: Ratio of toxic dose to therapeutic dose (TD50 / ED50)
explanation: Therapeutic index measures drug safety margin; higher index means safer drug.

title: Which class of antihypertensive drugs ends with the suffix '-pril' (e.g. Enalapril, Captopril)?
explanation: ACE (Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme) inhibitors typically share the suffix '-pril'.

title: What is an Agonist in pharmacology?
options: A drug that binds to a receptor and triggers a biological response
A drug that blocks receptor action
A drug that neutralizes stomach acid
explanation: Agonists activate receptors to elicit a full or partial maximal biological response.

title: Which test evaluates tablet resistance to mechanical shock during transport/packaging?
explanation: Roche Friabilator measures percentage weight loss of tablets under tumbling shock.

title: Which hormone is secreted by beta cells of Islets of Langerhans in pancreas?
explanation: Pancreatic beta cells synthesize and release insulin to lower blood glucose levels.

title: What is the mechanism of action of Loop Diuretics like Furosemide?
options: Inhibition of Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter in Thick Ascending Limb of Loop of Henle
Blocking sodium channels in distal tubule
explanation: Furosemide blocks Na+/K+/2Cl- symporters to increase urinary excretion of sodium and water.

title: What is Phytochemistry?
options: Study of phytochemical chemicals derived from plants
explanation: Phytochemistry analyzes secondary plant metabolites (alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenes).

title: Which equipment is used for moist heat sterilization under pressure?
explanation: Autoclaves sterilize equipment using saturated steam at 121°C under 15 psi pressure.

title: What is an Emulsion in pharmaceutics?
options: A biphasic liquid system of two immiscible liquids stabilized by emulsifying agent
explanation: Emulsions disperse fine liquid droplets (oil-in-water or water-in-oil) using emulsifiers.

title: Which vitamin is chemically known as Ascorbic Acid?
explanation: Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble antioxidant that prevents Scurvy.

title: What is First-Pass Metabolism?
options: Pre-systemic metabolism of oral drugs in liver and gut wall before reaching blood
explanation: First-pass effect metabolizes orally ingested drugs before systemic circulation entry.

title: Which opioid antagonist is used to treat acute Heroin / Morphine overdose?
explanation: Naloxone competitively displaces opioids from mu-receptors to reverse respiratory depression.

title: What does 'b.i.d.' stand for in medical prescriptions?
explanation: Bis in die (b.i.d.) translates to twice daily dosing.

title: Which organ excretes water-soluble drug metabolites primarily?
explanation: Renal glomeruli filter polar water-soluble drugs into urine for elimination.

title: What is the active constituent of Opium poppy latex causing pain relief?
explanation: Papaver somniferum latex yields morphine, a potent opioid analgesic.

title: What does GMP stand for in pharmaceutical manufacturing?
explanation: GMP regulations ensure products are consistently produced according to quality standards.

title: Which class of drugs lowers blood cholesterol by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase?
explanation: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis.

title: What is a Suppository?
options: Solid dosage form inserted into body orifices (rectum/vagina) where it melts
explanation: Suppositories melt at body temperature (37°C) to release local or systemic drugs.

title: Which mineral deficiency causes the 'Khaira disease' in rice crops?
explanation: Zinc deficiency causes rusty spots and growth stunting in paddy (rice) crops.

title: Which soil horizon is commonly referred to as Topsoil?
explanation: A Horizon is rich in organic humus and microorganisms, forming fertile topsoil.

title: What is the primary plant nutrient responsible for vegetative green growth and leaf development?
explanation: Nitrogen promotes chlorophyll synthesis and vigorous vegetative leafy growth.

title: Which cropping system grows two or more crops simultaneously on the same field in definite rows?
explanation: Intercropping arranges distinct crops in row patterns to maximize resource utilization.

title: What is the scientific name of Bread Wheat?
explanation: Triticum aestivum is hexaploid bread wheat cultivated globally.

title: Which bacterial genus forms symbiotic nitrogen-fixing root nodules in leguminous crops?
explanation: Rhizobium bacteria fix atmospheric N2 into ammonia inside legume root nodules.

title: What is the Green Revolution in India associated with?
options: High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds and agricultural technology
explanation: M.S. Swaminathan led Green Revolution introducing semi-dwarf wheat/rice varieties.

title: Which method of irrigation delivers water directly to plant root zones with minimal loss?
explanation: Drip irrigation provides micro-tubing drops directly at roots, saving over 50% water.

title: What is soil pH value range for neutral fertile soil?
explanation: Slightly acidic to neutral pH (6.5 - 7.5) optimizes nutrient bioavailability to crops.

title: Which crop disease is caused by Phytophthora infestans fungus?
explanation: Late Blight of Potato caused the historic 1845 Irish Potato Famine.

title: What is the process of removing excess water from agricultural land called?
explanation: Surface or sub-surface drainage removes waterlogging to prevent root aeration loss.

title: Which plant hormone promotes fruit ripening?
explanation: Ethylene gas acts as a natural ripening hormone in bananas, tomatoes, and apples.

title: What is Vermicomposting?
options: Composting using earthworms to break down organic waste
explanation: Eisenia fetida earthworms digest organic waste into nutrient-rich vermicompost castings.

title: Which weed is known as 'King of Weeds' in India?
explanation: Parthenium (Carrot grass) is an invasive toxic weed spreading rapidly across land.

title: What is the primary objective of Crop Rotation?
options: Prevent soil nutrient depletion and break pest life cycles
explanation: Rotating crops restores soil fertility balance and disrupts host-specific crop pests.

title: Which instrument measures soil moisture tension?
explanation: Tensiometers measure matric suction potential of soil water available to roots.

title: What is 'Kharif' cropping season in India?
options: Monsoon season crop sown in June-July and harvested in Oct-Nov
Winter season crop sown in Oct-Nov
explanation: Kharif crops (Rice, Maize, Cotton) depend on South-West monsoon rainfall.

title: What is 'Rabi' crop example in India?
explanation: Rabi crops (Wheat, Mustard, Barley) grow during winter harvest months.

title: Which biofertilizer fixes nitrogen in water fern Azolla in paddy fields?
explanation: Anabaena cyanobacteria symbiotic with Azolla fern enriches paddy nitrogen levels.

title: What is the term for washing out soluble soil nutrients into deeper layers by water?
explanation: Leaching carries dissolved nitrates and minerals below root zone due to heavy percolation.

title: Which plant tissue conducts water and mineral salts from roots to leaves?
explanation: Xylem vessel elements transport water unidirectionally upwards.

title: What is 'Minimum Support Price' (MSP) in Indian Agriculture?
options: Guaranteed minimum price set by government to purchase crops from farmers
explanation: MSP protects agricultural producers against sharp drops in farm market prices.

title: Which soil type has highest water holding capacity?
explanation: Clay particles have tiny pore spaces and high surface area, retaining maximum water.

title: What is 'Silviculture'?
options: Art and science of cultivating forest trees
explanation: Silviculture manages forest establishment, growth, composition, and timber harvest.

title: What causes 'Black heart' physiological disorder in stored potatoes?
explanation: Poor ventilation and sub-optimal O2 levels cause internal tuber tissue asphyxiation.

title: Which pest attacks cotton bolls causing severe economic yield losses?
explanation: Pectinophora gossypiella (Pink Bollworm) larvae bore into cotton bolls.

title: What is 'Hydroponics'?
options: Growing plants without soil using mineral nutrient solutions in water
Growing plants in dry desert sand
explanation: Hydroponics cultivates crops in inert media receiving dissolved aqueous nutrients.

title: Which enzyme breaks down starch into simple maltose sugars during seed germination?
explanation: Alpha and beta amylase enzymes hydrolyze endosperm starch reserve into sugars.

title: What is the C:N ratio of ideal organic compost soil manure?
explanation: A 10:1 to 12:1 C:N ratio indicates fully decomposed stable humus ready for microbes.

title: Which state is known as the 'Granary of India' or 'Bread Basket of India'?
explanation: Punjab produces high surplus wheat and paddy crops due to canal networks.

title: What is the derivative of sin(x) with respect to x?
explanation: The rate of change of sin(x) is cos(x).

title: What is the determinant of a 2x2 identity matrix [[1,0],[0,1]]?
What is the value of Laplace transform L{1}?
explanation: L{1} = integral from 0 to infinity of e^(-st) dt = 1/s for s > 0.

title: What is the order and degree of the differential equation (d^2y/dx^2)^3 + (dy/dx)^4 + y = 0?
explanation: Order is highest derivative (2); degree is power of highest order derivative (3).

title: What is the value of lim (x->0) [sin(x) / x]?
explanation: Standard limit theorem proves lim x->0 sin(x)/x = 1.

title: What are the eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix?
explanation: The roots of det(A - lambda*I) = 0 for diagonal matrices equal its main diagonal elements.

title: What is Euler's formula relating complex exponential to trigonometric functions?
explanation: Euler formula states e^(ix) = cos(x) + i*sin(x).

title: What is the integral of 1/x dx?
explanation: d/dx (ln|x|) = 1/x, so integral of 1/x is natural logarithm ln|x| + C.

title: According to Cayley-Hamilton Theorem, every square matrix satisfies what?
explanation: Cayley-Hamilton states p(A) = 0 where p(lambda) is the characteristic polynomial of A.

title: What is the rank of a 3x3 matrix with all zero entries?
explanation: The zero matrix has 0 linearly independent rows or columns, so rank = 0.

title: What is Fourier Series used for?
options: Representing periodic functions as sums of sines and cosines
explanation: Fourier expansion decomposes periodic signals into harmonic sine/cosine components.

title: What is the value of i^4 (where i = sqrt(-1))?
What condition must hold for a vector field F to be conservative?
explanation: A conservative vector field has zero curl (irrotational) and path-independent line integrals.

title: What is the Taylor series expansion of e^x centered at x = 0?
Which numerical method is used for finding roots of differentiable functions iteratively?
explanation: Newton-Raphson updates x_(n+1) = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n) with quadratic convergence.

title: What is Simpson's 1/3 Rule used for?
explanation: Simpson's 1/3 rule approximates definite integrals by fitting parabolas across intervals.

title: What is the gradient of a scalar function f(x,y,z)?
options: Vector of partial derivatives [df/dx, df/dy, df/dz]
explanation: grad(f) is a vector pointing in direction of greatest rate of increase of f.

title: If A and B are independent events, what is P(A and B)?
explanation: For independent events, joint probability equals product of marginal probabilities.

title: What is the mean of a Poisson distribution with parameter lambda?
explanation: Both mean and variance of a Poisson distribution equal lambda.

title: What is Green's Theorem in a plane?
options: Relates line integral around closed curve C to double integral over region D
explanation: Green's theorem converts vector line integrals around C into area integrals over enclosed D.

title: What is the solution of differential equation dy/dx = y?
explanation: Separating variables dy/y = dx gives ln(y) = x + c, so y = C*e^x.

title: What is a symmetric matrix?
options: A matrix equal to its transpose (A = A^T)
explanation: A symmetric matrix satisfies a_ij = a_ji for all i, j.

title: What is the period of function f(x) = sin(2x)?
explanation: Period of sin(kx) is 2*pi / k; for k=2, Period = 2*pi / 2 = pi.

title: What is the value of Gamma function Gamma(1/2)?
explanation: Gamma(1/2) = integral from 0 to inf of t^(-1/2) e^(-t) dt = sqrt(pi).

title: What is the divergence of a vector field F = [P, Q, R]?
explanation: Divergence is scalar dot product del . F = dP/dx + dQ/dy + dR/dz.

title: What is a singular matrix?
options: A square matrix with determinant equal to 0
explanation: A matrix is singular iff det(A) = 0 (it has no matrix inverse).

title: What is L'Hopital's Rule used for evaluating?
options: Indeterminate limits of type 0/0 or inf/inf
explanation: L'Hopital evaluates limits by taking derivatives of numerator and denominator.

title: What is the Z-transform used for in signal processing?
explanation: Z-transform converts discrete-time domain signals into complex frequency domain.

title: What is the value of 0! (Zero factorial)?
explanation: By mathematical convention and gamma function continuity, 0! = 1.

title: What is the total area under a standard normal distribution (Gaussian) curve?
explanation: Total probability density integral over all real values equals 1.

title: In operating systems, deadlocks can be prevented by breaking which Coffman condition?
explanation: Invalidating any 1 of the 4 Coffman conditions prevents deadlocks.

title: In Invertis B.Tech End-Sem exam pattern, how many total sections are typically present in a 70-mark paper?
options: Section A, B, C, and D
explanation: Standard semester papers feature 3 sections: Short Qs (Sec A), Medium Qs (Sec B), Long Qs (Sec C).

title: Which data structure is utilized in recursive function calls on the system call stack?
explanation: Recursion uses the system runtime stack to save stack frames and activation records.

title: In Object Oriented Programming, constructor overloading is an example of what?
explanation: Method/Constructor overloading is resolved statically at compile time.

title: Which memory management technique divides physical memory into fixed-size blocks called frames?
explanation: Paging allocates physical memory in fixed-size frames matching virtual page sizes.

title: What is the chromatic number of a complete graph K5?
explanation: A complete graph K_n requires n colors as every vertex is connected to every other.

title: Which register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be executed by CPU?
explanation: PC holds the memory address of the next instruction in sequence.

title: What is the primary key constraint requirement in SQL databases?
explanation: Primary Key uniquely identifies each row and strictly disallows null values.

title: Which protocol operates at Application Layer to transfer files between host and server?
explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) transfers files over TCP connections.

title: What is the time complexity of Quick Select algorithm for finding k-th smallest element on average?
explanation: Quick Select achieves O(n) average time complexity by pruning one sub-array partition.

title: Which logic gate is known as a Universal Gate?
explanation: NAND and NOR gates can implement any Boolean logic function without other gate types.

title: In software engineering, what does the Waterfall model emphasize?
explanation: Waterfall proceeds sequentially through requirement, design, coding, testing, and maintenance.

title: Which algorithm resolves page faults using LRU policy?
explanation: LRU replaces the page that has not been referenced for the longest duration.

title: What is the hamming distance between binary strings 10111 and 10001?
explanation: The strings differ at positions 3 and 4 (2 bit positions difference).

title: Which transmission medium has the highest bandwidth capacity and immunity to electromagnetic interference?
explanation: Optical fiber transmits light pulses through glass strands unaffected by EMI.

title: In compiler design, intermediate code generation typically uses which representation?
explanation: TAC uses at most three operands per instruction for machine-independent optimization.

title: What is the complement of a tautology proposition in Boolean logic?
explanation: The negation of a statement that is always true is a statement that is always false (contradiction).

title: Which CPU register holds the current instruction being executed?
explanation: IR stores the instruction code fetched from memory during execution.

title: What is the maximum number of edges in an undirected simple graph with n vertices?
explanation: In a complete simple graph K_n, total edges = n C 2 = n(n-1)/2.

title: Which design pattern handles communication between decoupled objects through a central hub?
explanation: Mediator encapsulates interaction between a set of colleague objects.

title: What is the worst-case time complexity of Insertion Sort?
explanation: Reverse sorted array requires n(n-1)/2 comparisons, resulting in O(n^2) worst case.

title: Which protocol resolves an IP address to a physical MAC hardware address?
explanation: ARP broadcasts IP queries on LAN to resolve matching MAC physical addresses.

title: What is the purpose of a Foreign Key in Relational Database Schema?
options: Enforces referential integrity between two tables
explanation: Foreign Keys link records in child table to primary key in parent table.

title: In Turing Machines, what is the 'Halting Problem'?
options: Undecidable problem of determining whether an arbitrary program will stop running
explanation: Alan Turing proved no general algorithm can decide if any program halts.

title: Which scheduling algorithm suffers from the Convoy Effect?
explanation: In FCFS, long CPU-bound processes block short I/O-bound processes behind them.

title: What is the height of a tree with only 1 root node?
explanation: A single node root tree has edge height 0 by standard convention.

title: Which layer of OSI model manages end-to-end flow control and error recovery?
explanation: Transport Layer (Layer 4) ensures end-to-end reliability and flow control.

title: In Automata theory, deterministic finite automata (DFA) can recognize which languages?
explanation: DFAs and NFAs precisely accept the class of Regular Languages.

title: What is a 'B-Tree' optimized for in database storage systems?
options: Reading and writing large blocks of memory on secondary disk storage
explanation: B-Trees keep disk I/O low by maintaining high branching factor node pages.

title: Which cipher technique substitutes each plaintext letter by shifting a fixed number of positions?
explanation: Caesar shift cipher replaces letters by a fixed shift offset down the alphabet.

title: If 5 workers complete a task in 12 days, how many days will 6 workers take at the same pace?
explanation: Total work = 5 * 12 = 60 man-days. Days for 6 workers = 60 / 6 = 10 days.

title: Find the next number in sequence: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
explanation: Differences are +4, +6, +8, +10, so next difference is +12. 30 + 12 = 42.

title: A train 150m long passes a telegraph pole in 9 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
A trader buys an item for Rs 400 and sells it for Rs 500. What is the profit percentage?
What is the average of first 50 natural numbers?
In a class of 60 students, the ratio of boys to girls is 3:2. How many girls are in the class?
explanation: Total ratio parts = 5. Girls = (2/5) * 60 = 24.

title: If a sum doubles itself at Simple Interest in 8 years, what is the rate of interest per annum?
If 'CAT' is coded as 3120, how is 'DOG' coded in the same scheme?
explanation: Positions in alphabet: C=3, A=1, T=20 (3120). D=4, O=15, G=7 (4157).

title: A tank can be filled by Pipe A in 4 hours and Pipe B in 6 hours. How long will both take together?
explanation: Combined rate = 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 per hr. Time = 12/5 = 2.4 hours.

title: What is the probability of getting a sum of 7 when rolling two unbiased 6-sided dice?
If 20% of a number is 80, what is 45% of that number?
A man travels 60 km at 30 km/h and returns at 20 km/h. What is his average speed for the round trip?
Find the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100, 125, 216
explanation: All numbers are perfect cubes (2^3, 3^3, 4^3, 5^3, 6^3) except 100 (10^2).

title: If A is B's sister, C is B's mother, D is C's father. How is A related to D?
explanation: A is daughter of C, and D is father of C, so A is D's granddaughter.

title: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand of a clock at 3:30?
In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'LEADER' be arranged?
explanation: Total letters = 6, E repeats 2 times. Ways = 6! / 2! = 720 / 2 = 360.

title: What is the compound interest on Rs 10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually?
If a clock strikes 6 times in 5 seconds, how many seconds will it take to strike 12 times?
explanation: 6 strikes have 5 intervals taking 5s (1s per interval). 12 strikes have 11 intervals = 11 seconds.

title: Two numbers are in ratio 3:4. Their LCM is 180. What is the smaller number?
explanation: Let numbers be 3x and 4x. LCM = 12x = 180 => x = 15. Smaller number = 3 * 15 = 45.

title: A bag contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. If two balls are drawn at random, what is probability both are blue?
If 15 men can build a wall in 20 days, how many men are required to build it in 12 days?
explanation: Men * Days = constant. 15 * 20 = M * 12 => M = 300 / 12 = 25 men.

title: Point A is 10 km West of Point B. Point C is 10 km South of Point B. What is the direct distance from A to C?
explanation: Form right triangle with legs 10 and 10. Hypotenuse = sqrt(10^2 + 10^2) = 10*sqrt(2) km.

title: A single discount equivalent to two successive discounts of 20% and 10% is:
If 3x + 2y = 12 and x - y = 1, what is the value of x?
explanation: From second eq y = x - 1. Substitute: 3x + 2(x - 1) = 12 => 5x - 2 = 12 => 5x = 14 => x = 2.8.

title: What is the HCF of 36, 54, and 90?
explanation: Factors: 36=18*2, 54=18*3, 90=18*5. Highest common factor = 18.

title: If January 1, 2024 was a Monday, what day of the week was January 1, 2025? (2024 is leap year)
explanation: Leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 odd days. Monday + 2 days = Wednesday.

title: A rectangular garden is 20m long and 15m wide. What is the length of its diagonal?
By selling an article for Rs 144, a man loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 10%?
explanation: Cost Price = 144 / 0.9 = Rs 160. Target selling price = 160 * 1.1 = Rs 176.

title: How many 3-digit numbers are completely divisible by 7?
If 'RED' is written as 27 and 'BLUE' as 40, what is the value of 'PINK'?
explanation: Sum of positions: P(16)+I(9)+N(14)+K(11) = 50.

title: What transformer architecture mechanism powers Modern LLMs like GPT and Gemini?
explanation: Self-Attention enables models to weight relationships between all tokens across long contexts.

title: Which organization created the open-source Linux kernel in 1991?
explanation: Linus Torvalds released the initial Linux kernel while studying at University of Helsinki.

title: What does RAG stand for in Generative AI architectures?
explanation: RAG combines vector search retrieval with generative LLMs to ground answers in external documents.

title: Which company developed the Quantum Computer chip named 'Sycamore'?
explanation: Google AI Quantum created the 53-qubit Sycamore processor demonstrating quantum supremacy in 2019.

title: What does CUDA stand for in NVIDIA GPU computing?
explanation: CUDA enables parallel computing processing directly on NVIDIA GPU hardware cores.

title: What is the primary consensus mechanism used by Bitcoin blockchain?
explanation: Bitcoin relies on SHA-256 Proof of Work mining to validate block transactions.

title: Which technology enables lightweight containerized application deployment?
explanation: Docker isolates applications inside lightweight container runtimes sharing the host OS kernel.

title: What does WebAssembly (Wasm) enable inside web browsers?
options: Running high-performance compiled code (C++/Rust) at near-native speed
explanation: Wasm runs binary instruction formats in modern browser engines alongside JS.

title: What is the activation function commonly used in deep neural network hidden layers to prevent vanishing gradients?
explanation: ReLU (f(x)=max(0,x)) computes fast and prevents vanishing gradient problems during backpropagation.

title: Which open-source container orchestration tool was created by Google and maintained by CNCF?
explanation: Kubernetes (K8s) automates deployment, scaling, and management of containerized workloads.

title: What does JSON-LD stand for in modern web data structuring?
options: JavaScript Object Notation for Linked Data
explanation: JSON-LD structures linked data for search engine schema indexing.

title: Which protocol provides real-time bi-directional low-latency communication over a single TCP connection?
explanation: WebSockets establish full-duplex persistent connections between browser and server.

title: What is a Vector Database (e.g. Pinecone, Chroma, Milvus) optimized for?
options: Searching high-dimensional embedding vectors by cosine similarity
explanation: Vector DBs index semantic embeddings to perform rapid nearest-neighbor (k-NN) retrieval.

title: What is 'Zero Trust Architecture' in cybersecurity?
options: Never trust, always verify every user and device request regardless of location
Trusting internal corporate Wi-Fi network automatically
explanation: Zero Trust assumes network threats exist everywhere and requires continuous authentication.

title: Which company developed the TypeScript programming language?
explanation: Anders Hejlsberg led TypeScript development at Microsoft, releasing it in 2012.

title: What is the main advantage of Solid-State Drives (SSD) over Hard Disk Drives (HDD)?
options: No moving mechanical parts and faster read/write I/O speed
explanation: NAND flash memory in SSDs eliminates mechanical latency for instant data access.

title: What is a 'Diffusion Model' in generative AI (e.g. Stable Diffusion, Midjourney)?
options: A model that generates images by removing noise from random latent vectors
explanation: Diffusion models learn to reverse a gradual noise process to construct clear images.

title: Which wireless standard operates in the 6 GHz frequency band?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6E extends Wi-Fi 6 into 6 GHz spectrum for lower latency and wider channels.

title: What is 'Edge Computing'?
options: Processing data closer to the source device rather than relying solely on distant cloud servers
explanation: Edge computing reduces latency and bandwidth by running computations near data sensors.

title: Which JavaScript engine powers Google Chrome and Node.js runtime?
explanation: V8 compiles JavaScript into native machine code for Chrome and Node.js.

title: What does fine-tuning LoRA stand for in LLM efficient adaptation?
explanation: LoRA freezes pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices.

title: What is 'GraphQL' developed by Meta?
options: A query language for APIs providing clients exact data request control
explanation: GraphQL allows clients to request exactly what they need in a single query endpoint.

title: Which cloud computing service model provides virtualized servers, storage, and networking (e.g. AWS EC2)?
explanation: IaaS delivers fundamental computing infrastructure resources on demand.

title: What is the purpose of a Reverse Proxy (e.g. NGINX)?
options: Sits in front of web servers to handle load balancing, SSL termination, and caching
explanation: Reverse proxies direct client requests to destination backend servers securely.

title: What is the quantum phenomenon where two particles remain linked regardless of distance?
explanation: Entangled particle states cannot be described independently regardless of distance.

title: Which company developed the Flutter cross-platform UI framework?
explanation: Google launched Flutter using the Dart language to build native mobile/desktop apps.

title: What does OAuth 2.0 handle in web applications?
options: Authorization delegation without sharing user passwords
explanation: OAuth 2.0 grants third-party applications limited access to HTTP user accounts via tokens.

title: What is a 'Zero-Day Vulnerability'?
options: A software security flaw unknown to the vendor with 0 days to patch before exploitation
A vulnerability that expires in 24 hours
A bug introduced on day 0 of coding
explanation: Zero-day flaws are exploited by hackers before developers create a security patch.

title: What does ML-KEM / Kyber refer to in modern cryptography?
explanation: NIST selected ML-KEM (Kyber) to protect against future quantum computer decryption.

title: Which open-source version control system was developed to manage Linux kernel development?
explanation: Linus Torvalds created Git in 2005 for distributed velocity in Linux kernel development.
